patterns: Registry pattern: one languages/<lang>.rs module with pub const *_QUERY strings plus optional extract_* handlers, registered by a match arm in get_language_info() (LanguageInfo struct) and get_ts_language() (Language only), and an extension row in lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP.

Capture-name contract: ELEMENT_QUERY uses @function/@class with inner @func_name|@method_name|@class_name captures; CALL_QUERY uses @call; IMPORT_QUERY uses @import_path; DEFUSE_QUERY uses @write.*, @read.*, @writeread.* prefixes (parser_elements.rs 282-300, 495, 577, 878-882).

Java defuse pattern: `(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)`, `(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)`, `(identifier) @read.usage`, with read captures de-duplicated by byte offset against writes (parser_elements.rs 890).

Inheritance handler contract: fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> returning prefixed strings ('extends X', 'implements X'); Java walks named fields (superclass, interfaces), Swift walks children by kind; cpp.rs and csharp.rs also define extract_inheritance (not read in detail). The handler is called only for class nodes (parser_elements.rs 398-410).

Fallback import handling: extract_imports_from_node stores the full captured node text as module when no kind-specific arm matches (parser_elements.rs `_` arm), which is how Java import_declaration and Swift import_declaration are currently handled.

css wiring precedent: the grammar's crate is declared in the root and crate Cargo.toml, its extension is added to EXTENSION_MAP, its module is declared, and it gets a get_language_info arm and a get_ts_language arm. Queries with no consumer use None (defuse_query: None, extract_inheritance: None).

approaches.name: A: Java-pattern full handler (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs modelled on java.rs: ELEMENT_QUERY over function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration; CALL_QUERY over function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression; REFERENCE_QUERY over named_type; IMPORT_QUERY over namespace_use_clause; DEFUSE_QUERY using variable_name (see defuse_query_draft); extract_inheritance walking unfielded base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 into root and core Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, mod declaration, get_language_info arm (defuse_query Some, extract_inheritance Some, extract_function_name None), get_ts_language arm. Add unit tests in php.rs, one integration test file, and README update.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including DEFUSE and inheritance
Java and Swift give a tested pattern for each handler
Queries are verified against the grammar's node-types.json and grammar.json, so the risk is in query compilation only
Stays inside the scope listed in the issue
cons: Imports are stored as raw clause text (module = 'App\\Models\\User', items empty) via the fallback arm, not split into module and items
Group use (`use A\\{B, C}`) loses the group prefix at clause level
Unit-test count is the largest of the three approaches

approaches.name: B: Registry-only minimum (scope cut)
approaches.description: Wire tree-sitter-php and the registry with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only, following the css.rs shape: REFERENCE_QUERY None, DEFUSE_QUERY None, extract_inheritance None. Ship the element, call and import outputs; defer defuse and inheritance.
pros: Smallest change and fastest path to a registered language
Lowest risk of query or handler bugs
cons: Fails the issue's acceptance criteria: extract_inheritance and DEFUSE_QUERY are required by the issue's Scope and Acceptance Criteria

approaches.name: C: Structured imports via a core arm
approaches.description: Approach A plus a new `"namespace_use_declaration"` (or `"namespace_use_clause"`) arm in parser_elements.rs extract_imports_from_node (near line 142, beside the import_from_statement arm), so PHP imports become ImportInfo { module: 'App\\Models', items: ['User'] } instead of raw text.
pros: Structured import output matching Python's import_from_statement handling
Cleaner module and item names for downstream consumers
Group use prefixes can be handled correctly
cons: Changes shared core code in parser_elements.rs, which is outside the issue's listed scope (AGENTS.md: do not modify files outside scope)
Needs its own test and review, adding roughly 1 to 2 days
The new arm is kind-specific, so existing language extraction is unchanged

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies every acceptance criterion in #1864 (DEFUSE_QUERY, extract_inheritance, element, call and import queries, and the mixed-HTML parse) while staying inside the issue's listed scope. Use LANGUAGE_PHP, use clause-level IMPORT_QUERY for cleaner module text, and document that imports are raw clause text. Treat Approach C as a follow-up issue, because it touches parser_elements.rs outside the listed scope. Note that the issue says external PRs are not accepted, so this is for the in-house team.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Grammar source inspected: php/src/grammar.json (rules) and php/src/node-types.json (fields/children), both from tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php master.
1. class_declaration rule (grammar.json): SEQ[CHOICE[FIELD(attributes=attribute_list)|BLANK], REPEAT(_modifier), ALIAS(class), FIELD(name=name), CHOICE[base_clause|BLANK], CHOICE[class_interface_clause|BLANK], FIELD(body=declaration_list)]. The clauses are NOT fields: there is no child_by_field_name("superclass") or ("interfaces"). Walk them by kind over node.child(i).
2. extends: a child with kind "base_clause" (rule: SEQ[ALIAS "extends", SEQ[_name, REPEAT(SEQ[",", _name])]]). node-types.json children of base_clause: name | qualified_name | relative_name, multiple=true, required=true. For each named child of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name, emit format!("extends {text}") where text = source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()].
3. implements: a child with kind "class_interface_clause" (rule: SEQ[ALIAS "implements", SEQ[_name, REPEAT(SEQ[",", _name])]]). Same children set (name | qualified_name | relative_name). Emit format!("implements {text}") per named child, in source order.
4. Leaf type: the grammar rule for name is a PATTERN (identifier-like regex), so the leaf kind is "name", not Java's "type_identifier". Qualified names (e.g. \\Base\\Model) are a qualified_name node whose text includes the namespace prefix.
5. No clauses: neither child kind is present, so the result is an empty Vec.
Expected for "class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}": ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"].
